paragraphs.source_en: We cannot let our lives be “dreams deferred,” as Langston Hughes wrote in his famous poem, “Harlem.” It’s time to let your dreams speak—even as you still have to put food on the table and pay off debts. Dreaming once again does not mean absolving ourselves of financial responsibilities. It means reviving our dreams as juice for the journey.

paragraphs.source_en: A few years after graduating from college, **Grant Sabatier** had his wake-up call when he discovered he hadn’t enough money to buy a burrito. He was living with his parents, a classic failure-to-launch millennial. That was when he decided that he was going to make $1 million by age thirty. He says the first thing he needed to do was change his mind-set to one of saving—which he refers to as paying yourself first. He took a screenshot of his measly bank balance, set the goal of having $1 million in assets in five years, and immediately started educating himself*.*
